description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by walking perldiag's RUN-TIME fatals (USER question 3: "what does perl die on that PCL lets through?").  ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/q3/fatals.pl: 67 cases, each in its own `eval {}`, ONLY died-vs-lived compared (exact text is not a goal); fatals.perl / fatals.pcl.  50 rows agree (every method-resolution error, undefined sub, division/modulus by zero, sqrt/log domain, hashref-as-array and the other CROSS-TYPE ref errors, missing module, die objects, die in sort/map, pack/unpack bad template, substr lvalue outside string, control-flow errors).  PERL DIES, PCL LIVES (the dangerous direction -- a program that validates with eval, or relies on the die to stop, carries on with garbage):

    string as ARRAY ref / HASH ref / SCALAR ref under `use strict`     (strict refs is not enforced at run time at all -- grep DECIDED / not-supported.md first: if ruled, cite it and CLOSE this row)
    number as ARRAY ref (`$num->[0]`)          deref undef as ARRAY in RVALUE context (`my @x = @$undef`)
    modify a read-only value: `for my $x (1) { $x = 2 }`, `$_++ for (1, 2)`, `for ("abc") { chop }`
    INVALID REGEX at run time: `my $p = "(unclosed"; "x" =~ /$p/` and `"*abc"` -- the `eval { qr/$user_input/ }` validation idiom cannot work
    `require FILE` whose last statement is false          `bless "str", "Klass"` (non-reference)
    `exists $h->{k}{j}{i}` through a NON-ref value (strict refs again)       `unpack("x5 a", "ab")` ('x' outside of string)       `local $/ = \0`
  PCL DIES, PERL LIVES (1): `keys %$undef` in rvalue context.
Order by how ordinary: invalid-regex (validation idiom) > read-only modification (a silent no-op hides real bugs) > strict refs (RULING needed: enforcing it costs a check per symbolic deref -- measure) > `@$undef` rvalue > the rest.  Each fix is small and runtime-side; rule 12 applies (these ARE missing cases that fall through).  Guard: the battery itself as a Pl/t file (died/lived table, perl as oracle at authoring time).


=== USER RULING s494 (2026-09-21) -- this task's PRIORITY goes UP ===
USER, s494 (2026-09-21): "It is OK if errors aren't the same as Perl, as long as they fail in the same places. But we don't want it to be horribly messy either. :-)"
"Fail in the same places" is the USER's stated bar for errors, and this task is the list of places where PCL does NOT fail and perl does (16 run-time fatals PCL lives through: strict refs never enforced, `@$undef` rvalue, read-only modification, ...).  By that bar these outrank every message-text task.  Text stays free: when one of these is made to die, any readable one-line message will do.

=== s495f (2026-09-25): the ONE everyday row (programs/nested-eval-errors) -- MEASURED, NOT SHIPPED (brief: strict-dependent = size only) ===
The row's first differing line 3 has TWO causes: `eval { my $u; my @a = @$u; ... }` must die (perl prints `strict-refs-died`, PCL `autoviv-rvalue-ok`), and `$SIG{__DIE__}` inside eval is never invoked (#1554, ruled/owned elsewhere) -- both would have to close for the row to read `same`.
THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (scratch/s495f/p-undef.pl, 41 cases, perl 5.40.3): the rvalue death of `@$undef` / `%$undef` / `$$undef` IS strict-DEPENDENT.  Under `no strict` all four LIVE in perl (undef is taken as the symbolic name "" -- an empty @{""}); under `use strict` they die "Can't use an undefined value as an ARRAY reference" -- in list assignment, join, scalar(@$u), sort, reverse, "@$u", (@$u, 1), boolean `if (@$u)` and `my ($a) = @$u`.  So there is no strict-independent subset to ship: the case IS strict refs.
The vivifying contexts that must KEEP living under strict (all probed, perl vivifies $u): push / unshift / splice @$u, $u->[0] = 1, @$u = (...), for (@$u), keys / values / each %$u, map / grep over @$u, $#$u, \@$u, @$u as a sub argument, slices @$u[0,1] / @$u{a}, pop / shift, exists $u->{a}{b}, and the RVALUE element reads $u->[0] / $u->{a}{b} (which vivify $u itself in perl, with or without strict).
SIZE of enforcing `strict refs` (the only way to close this row's first cause): (1) the pragma's LEXICAL scope at every deref site -- the mechanism EXISTS: Pl::Environment's per-scope `pragmas` frame already carries `strict_subs` and `use_integer` (Parser2.pm:858, Parser.pm:9377-9539), so a `strict_refs` key is one more entry at the same two sites, plus `no strict 'refs'` / `no strict` clearing it; (2) an emission marker on the RVALUE p-cast-@ / p-cast-% / p-cast-$ sites only -- today `(p-cast-@ $u)` is the SAME form under push (vivify) and under `my @a = @$u` (rvalue), so the ExprToCL deref emitter must pass its context (the vivify list above is the set that must NOT get the marker); (3) runtime: a strict arm that dies "Can't use an undefined value as an ARRAY reference" for undef and "Can't use string (\"x\") as an ARRAY ref while \"strict refs\" in use" for a string (the #2103 row 1 symbolic cases come with it for free), one type test per marked rvalue deref -- measure on a deref-heavy bench row (arrhash, slices, feread) before shipping.  Emission-changing => gen bump, corpus-diff read per file, full sweep: every perl-tests file that dereferences undef under strict and currently passes on the empty list is a candidate mover.  Estimate: one agent session.
FOUND WHILE PROBING (filed separately): #2341 -- on the raw-slot path `my $u; push @$u, 1` DIES ("Type of arg 1 to push must be array") and rvalue element reads / foreach / keys / slices / pop do not vivify the undef scalar they dereference (all right under PCL_OPT=-raw-slot).
everyday baseline row programs/nested-eval-errors: cause re-worded to name BOTH causes (#2103 strict refs + #1554 __DIE__); verdict and line unchanged.


=== s497b (2026-09-26): strict refs ENFORCED + most rows closed ===
SHIPPED: `strict 'refs'` as a LEXICAL fact (Pl::Parser::strict_refs_regions_of: source-location regions, explicit statement beats use VERSION >= 5.011, string eval inherits via the pseudo-feature strict_refs); deref-site markers :strict / :strict-lv / :rvalue on p-cast-@/%/$ and :strict on the element reads (ir-spec Â§3.2f); runtime arms die perl's two messages.  Fatals battery rows now agreeing: deref undef as ARRAY (rvalue), deref undef as HASH (the opposite row â keys lives now), string as ARRAY/HASH/SCALAR ref, number as ARRAY ref, modify read-only literal x3 (read-only literal boxes, with #1391), bless non-reference, unpack 'x' outside of string.  perl's t/lib/strict/refs: 26 of 33 cases agree died/lived (13 on 24422497).  Guards Pl/t/strict-refs-01.t (79) + Pl/t/fatals-01.t (85).
STILL OPEN (each in fatals-01.t's TODO block): `require` of a false-returning file (#1688 â needs the module's last value), the two invalid-regex rows (#2372, s496a), `exists` through a non-ref CHAIN (#2403), `local $/ = \0` (#2405).  Write path / code / glob strict: #2403; module-import strict: #2406.
subject: SILENT CONTINUATION: 16 run-time errors perl DIES on and PCL LIVES through -- strict refs never enforced (a STRING used as an ARRAY/HASH/SCALAR ref), `@$undef` rvalue, a NUMBER as an array ref, modification of a read-only value (3 spellings), an INVALID REGEX at run time (2), `require` of a false-returning file, `bless` of a non-reference, ...
